summary.summary: Calderdale ended 2025/26 with just £2.68m of external investments — a single NatWest call account, down from £6.2m a year earlier — against £137.6m of PWLB debt: the cash cushion is essentially gone. The report is unusually candid about why: years of SEND (schools funding) deficits and reserve drawdowns have worsened cashflow, forcing rolling short-term borrowing from other councils (£305k of interest in the year) even as £9.98m of PWLB debt matured without replacement. Treasury costs overran budget by £654k because investment income fell £1.54m short of plan. Internal borrowing will need replacing with new long-term PWLB loans in 2026/27, so a step-up in external debt is coming against a CFR of £237.3m.

signals.headline: External investments of £2.68m at 31 March 2026 (one NatWest call account; £6.2m a year earlier) against £137.6m of PWLB debt
signals.why: With almost no invested cash, day-to-day spending depends on continuously rolling short-term loans from other councils.

signals.headline: The SEND funding deficit 'accumulated over a number of years continued to significantly impact on the Council's cashflow throughout' 2025/26, driving increased short-term borrowing
signals.why: A schools deficit parked behind the statutory accounting override is being financed with real borrowed cash today.

signals.headline: 'Significant levels of Council reserves have been used' in recent years to fund additional costs and the increased SEND deficit, reducing balances and forcing short-term borrowing
signals.why: The cash that once backed reserves is spent, so internal borrowing capacity is exhausted and new pressure lands directly on external debt.

findings.paper_title: First Quarter Projected Outturn - Revenue and Capital Update 2026-27
findings.headline: Calderdale is borrowing £151.4m (40% of capital programme) while managing structural revenue overspends
findings.detail: The council's capital programme totals £371.8m, with £151.4m (40%) to be funded by borrowing. Over 50% (£195.9m) comes from government and external grants. The paper notes it will review 'the anticipated timing of borrowing, aligned to delivery of the Capital Programme' but does not yet show what the revenue cost of this borrowing will be.
findings.matters: A council with a £5.4m operating overspend and falling reserves is adding material borrowing costs to an already tight budget. The timing and interest rate assumption need to be clear.
findings.quote: Over 50% of the Capital Programme is funded through external and government grants (£195.9m). Borrowing represents 40% of funding with the remainder of the programme funded from revenue contribution and pooled resources (capital receipts generated by the sale of assets).

findings.paper_title: First Quarter Projected Outturn - Revenue and Capital Update 2026-27
findings.headline: Overall revenue overspend of £5.36m (1.89%) confirmed at Q1 with only partial mitigation expected
findings.detail: Calderdale approved a balanced budget of £282.96m but is forecasting year-end outturn of £288.5m, an overspend of £5.36m. The paper indicates directorates are developing recovery plans but does not show them. The council is relying on a contribution to general balances of £680k, implying further reserve depletion.
findings.matters: A Q1 overspend of nearly £5.4m with five months to run means the council is unlikely to deliver a balanced outturn without significant mid-year action. This is a governance and cash management issue.
findings.quote: There is currently a net overspend at year-end forecast on revenue budgets of £5.36m or 1.89%. The report provides a detailed breakdown of the overspend across service areas and sets out action that is being taken to reduce the overspend by the 31 March 2027.

findings.paper_title: First Quarter Projected Outturn - Revenue and Capital Update 2026-27
findings.headline: SEND High Needs deficit of £30.5m will impose a £11m liability on general balances from April 2028 when statutory override expires
findings.detail: Calderdale's SEND High Needs block is forecasting a £30.5m deficit (costs of £69m against DSG funding of £38.5m). The statutory override allowing this deficit to sit on the balance sheet ends 31 March 2028. The DfE will fund 90% of accumulated deficits; the remaining 10% (estimated £11m in 2028/29) must be funded from general balances, creating a known future cash demand.
findings.matters: A council with a known £11m liability landing on its reserves in two years needs to demonstrate plans to address it. If general balances fall below prudent levels before then, the council will face a cash crisis.
findings.figures: £30.5m High Needs deficit for 2026/27, £69m costs, £38.5m DSG funding, £11m estimated residual liability in 2028/29
findings.quote: The SEND High Needs budget was approved for 2026/27 with total costs estimated to be £69.0m and funding from the Dedicated Schools Grant (DSG) of £38.5m This resulted in a budgeted High Needs deficit of £30.5m... The residual 10% will require funding from general balances and not Dedicated Schools Grant, this is estimated to be £11m in 2028/29.

findings.paper_title: First Quarter Projected Outturn - Revenue and Capital Update 2026-27
findings.headline: Children's Social Care experiencing £1.57m pressure from complex, high-cost placements that are demand-led and cannot be reduced
findings.detail: Children's Social Care is forecasting a £1.57m overspend driven by a small number of children with complex needs requiring specialised interventions and placements. Because the Council has a statutory duty to safeguard children in care and support care leavers, this spending is demand-led and cannot be controlled without breaching legal obligations.
findings.matters: Demand-led statutory spending that is growing faster than budgeted signals a cash constraint on a core service the council cannot rationally reduce. A lender needs to know whether this is structural or temporary.
findings.figures: £1.57m forecast overspend within Children's Social Care budget
findings.quote: Children's Social Care continues to experience significant budgetary pressures arising from the increasing complexity of need presented by a small number of children requiring specialised interventions and placements... The combination of high-cost placements, increasing care package requirements, and rising costs associated with supporting care leavers has resulted in a forecast budget pressure of £1.57m.

findings.paper_title: First Quarter Projected Outturn - Revenue and Capital Update 2026-27
findings.headline: Adult Social Care overspend of £4.6m with demand accelerating and savings not landing
findings.detail: Calderdale is forecasting a £4.6m overspend in Adults and Wellbeing, its largest cost driver. Care home placements grew from 664 to 698 between February and August; Mental Health placements are up 31% and Learning Disability up 9%. Despite planned savings of £2.56m, only £291k (11%) has been delivered so far.
findings.matters: Adult social care is the hardest cost to control and signals structural budget weakness if demand and complexity continue. A lender would want to know how the council plans to arrest this or whether it expects sustained deficits.
findings.figures: £4.6m overspend (4.5%), care homes 664→698 placements, MH placements +31%, LD placements +9%, savings £291k of £2.56m target (11% delivered)
findings.quote: The principal overspend drivers in Adults and Wellbeing are rising costs and volumes of care home placements, particularly Older People, Learning Disability and Mental Health placements. Growth in care home numbers from 664 to 698 people between February and August 2026. Mental Health care home placements increasing by 31%. Learning Disability care home placements increasing by 9%.
